tradition: National Baptist (NBC USA / historically Black Baptist)

source_document.name: Articles of Faith, National Baptist Convention, USA, Inc. ("What We Believe")
source_document.original_url_status: 404 on 2026-09-19; nationalbaptist.com now serves only an event page. The Internet Archive snapshot of 2023-01-28 was opened and read instead.
source_document.date_note: The page prints no date. The eighteen articles are the text known as the New Hampshire Confession (1833; revised edition 1853). That attribution and those years are standard reference knowledge and were NOT read off the page opened; confirm before printing a date on the site.

cells.document: Articles of Faith, National Baptist Convention, USA, Inc.
cells.date: undated on the page (text of the New Hampshire Confession, 1833/1853; see source_document.date_note)
cells.section: Article VI, The Freeness of Salvation
cells.excerpt: the blessings of salvation are made free to all by the Gospel; that it is the immediate duty of all to accept them by cordial, penitent and obedient faith
cells.shows: Salvation is offered freely to everyone and each hearer is bound to accept it by faith, with only the person's own voluntary rejection standing in the way.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports, but weaker than 75 when read with Article IX (next cell)

cells.document: Articles of Faith, National Baptist Convention, USA, Inc.
cells.date: undated on the page (text of the New Hampshire Confession, 1833/1853; see source_document.date_note)
cells.section: Article IX, God's Purpose of Grace
cells.excerpt: election is the eternal purpose of God, according to which he graciously regenerates, sanctifies and saves sinners; that being perfectly consistent with the free agency of man
cells.shows: The same articles affirm God's eternal election and hold it together with human free agency; Article VII also says regeneration is effected by the Holy Spirit and Article XI that true believers endure to the end.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: weaker: the document itself sits nearer the middle than 75 (it affirms election, Spirit-wrought regeneration and perseverance alongside the free offer). The synergist lean of 75 reflects preaching and practice more than this text.

cells.document: Articles of Faith, National Baptist Convention, USA, Inc.
cells.date: undated on the page (text of the New Hampshire Confession, 1833/1853; see source_document.date_note)
cells.section: Article XIV, Baptism and the Lord's Supper
cells.excerpt: by the sacred use of bread and wine, are to commemorate together the dying love of Christ
cells.shows: The Supper is a commemoration kept by church members, and the same article calls baptism the immersion of a believer that shows forth faith 'in a solemn and beautiful emblem'.

The Articles of Faith do not address tongues, prophecy or healing; Article X speaks only of the Holy Spirit's sanctifying work through the word, self-examination and prayer. No convention statement or resolution on the sign gifts could be found and opened.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: none found (the coordinate of 35 cannot be cited to a primary document)

cells.document: Articles of Faith, National Baptist Convention, USA, Inc.
cells.date: undated on the page (text of the New Hampshire Confession, 1833/1853; see source_document.date_note)
cells.section: Article XVIII, The World to Come
cells.excerpt: at the last day, Christ will descend from heaven, and raise the dead from the grave for final retribution; that a solemn separation will then take place
cells.shows: The articles teach one return of Christ, a general resurrection and a final judgment at the last day, and say nothing of Israel and the church, a rapture, a tribulation or a millennium.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: weaker, arguably the other way: the text is silent on every dispensational distinctive and its single last-day scheme is not a dispensational one. The coordinate of 72 has no support in this document; no other convention statement on the question was found.

cells.document: Articles of Faith, National Baptist Convention, USA, Inc.
cells.date: undated on the page (text of the New Hampshire Confession, 1833/1853; see source_document.date_note)
cells.excerpt: the supreme standard by which all human conduct, creeds, and opinions shall be tried
cells.shows: The Bible is named the supreme standard, and creeds are listed among the things it judges.

cells.document: Articles of Faith, National Baptist Convention, USA, Inc.
cells.date: undated on the page (text of the New Hampshire Confession, 1833/1853; see source_document.date_note)
cells.excerpt: a congregation of baptized believers, associated by covenant in the faith and fellowship of the Gospel; observing the ordinances of Christ; governed by his laws
cells.shows: The church is defined as a self-covenanting local congregation governed by Christ's laws, with no liturgy, calendar or service book prescribed anywhere in the articles (Article XV asks only that the Lord's Day be kept).
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: weaker: consistent with free worship by what it omits, but the document makes no positive statement about the form of worship.

notes: One document serves every cell that could be filled: the eighteen Articles of Faith the National Baptist Convention, USA, Inc. published on its own site under 'What We Believe'. The live page returned 404 on 2026-09-19 (both the /about-nbc/ and the older /about-us/ URL; the linked PDF returned 406), so the Internet Archive snapshot of 2023-01-28 was opened and every excerpt was copied from it; the site should link to that archived URL or re-check the live site before publishing. The articles are public-domain nineteenth-century text, so nothing is link-only. 'binding' is false throughout: the convention is a fellowship of autonomous congregations and the articles are a representative statement, not a confession a church or member must subscribe. Grace: the tradition is not split institutionally, but the document is; two cells are given because Article VI (free offer, duty of all to believe) and Article IX (eternal election consistent with free agency) are both what holders would point to, and together they sit nearer the centre than the audited 75. Gifts: none found; the only description located of the convention's stance on charismatic practice was a Wikipedia article ('Bapticostal movement'), which is not a primary source and was not used. Kingdom: the only primary text found is non-dispensational in shape and silent on Israel and the church, so the audited 72 is unsupported by any document found. The page also carries a 'Statement of Religious Freedom' dated October 2010, which bears on none of the six axes. The date 1833/1853 for the underlying New Hampshire Confession was not read from the opened page and should be verified before it is printed.
